transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Emma Castillo (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (Head of MLOps, Stellan), Jon Park (Platform Eng), Lena Cho (CTO), Avery Singh (SRE)

Summary:
Quick recap of week-3 lab runs: Redwood ran three scenarios (latency-optimized, balanced, throughput-optimized) against Stellan's incumbent provider (CurrentVendorAI). Latency p95 improved in the latency-optimized run for short-form prompts, throughput sustained slightly higher for Redwood in the throughput profile. Discussion focused on KV cache warm-up, batching tradeoffs, and routing to smaller-quantized model variants during spikes. Next: share tuned configs and run a dedicated latency-only test with pinned model.

Topics covered:
- Benchmark numbers (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec)
- Observed variance in evening spike (12/24 logs)
- Tuning: batch sizes, continuous batching window, KV cache pre-warm, quantization profile
- Fallback/routing behavior when capacity constrained
- Security/KMS question and data residency note
- Next steps & owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma Castillo: all right, thanks everyone for jumping on, uh we'll keep this to an hour, maybe a little over. quick roll, who we've got?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: hi i'm marta, thanks. jon and avery are here from infra, lena'll pop in for the last ten.
[00:13] Jon Park: hey team.
[00:15] Ravi Patel: good afternoon, ravi from redwood se. we ran the sprint bench with three profiles, i'll start with the numbers then we can dig in.
[00:23] Ravi Patel: latency profile - pinned to redwood-opt-3b-q4, p50 about 28ms token, p95 140ms, p99 noisy about 300ms. incumbent p95 was 210ms on the same workload.
[00:36] Marta Ruiz: wait can you say the p95 again? 140ms vs 210?
[00:40] Ravi Patel: yep that's right, 140 for our run, 210 for current vendor, we saw about 33% improvement at p95 on short prompts.
[00:47] Jon Park: what's your test rig? like gpu type and batching?
[00:51] Ravi Patel: we used g5x2 equivalent, single inference node, continuous batching window 8ms, target batch 8 tokens. kernels selected to prefer fused-attention - note: on your side the incumbent had slightly higher cold-start since they use larger model shard sizes.
[01:05] Marta Ruiz: hmmm the evening spike, we saw a lot of variance - did you replicate a spike pattern?
[01:11] Ravi Patel: yes we replayed your 12/24 spike trace, during that replay the throughput run hit 3200 tokens/sec sustained, where incumbent peaked at 2800 tokens/sec. but we also saw a higher variance when cache cold.
[01:24] Avery Singh: that variance is what we worry about - our SLA is p95 under 250ms for critical requests. sometimes we saw p95 creep up late evening.
[01:33] Ravi Patel: that's expected when kv cache not warmed or when we route to a quantized fallback for cost optimization. we can change the prefix caching policy to keep top-10K prefixes resident; that removes most of the cold miss penalty but increases memory footprint.
[01:46] Emma Castillo: to clarify the tradeoff, keeping more prefixes warm increases OPEX a bit, but improves tail latency — could be worth it for your critical path.
[01:55] Jon Park: can we see the memory numbers if we warm 10k vs 2k?
[01:59] Ravi Patel: yes i'll upload the matrix. for 10k prefixes it's roughly +12GB on the node, 2k is +3GB.
[02:07] Marta Ruiz: ok, send that.
[02:09] Ravi Patel: also on quantization: we tested q3b and q4f variants. q3b gave ~1.6x throughput but p95 moved up ~30ms in steady state. q4f keeps latency low but costs more.
[02:22] Emma Castillo: how's accuracy? any regression with q3b?
[02:25] Ravi Patel: micro-regressions on rare tokens, we ran your eval set — rouge/emd differences were within noise for the customer intent extraction task. i'll include eval summary.
[02:35] Marta Ruiz: is that the standard eval set we gave you?
[02:38] Ravi Patel: yes, stella-intent-v1 set plus the two heavy prompts you flagged.
[02:42] Jon Park: about routing and fallback — can we bail to incumbent if redwood is saturated?
[02:47] Noah Kim: yes, you can set routing policy to prefer redwood but fallback to incumbent or lower-cost variant. we can demo policy during next call.
[02:55] Lena Cho: quick security q — KMS integration, can we use our HSM?
[02:59] Emma Castillo: absolutely, for private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for hosted we integrate with major clouds KMS and can support key import for dedicated. we'll share the security brief.
[03:09] Marta Ruiz: and audit logs? we need per-token tracing for compliance; can redwood provide that level of detail?
[03:15] Noah Kim: yes, token-level traces are available in console for the dedicated plan, and we can export audit logs to your S3/secure bucket.
[03:23] Avery Singh: about that 12/24 spike you mentioned — we noticed a pod OOM and then a restart, might be why latency spiked.
[03:29] Ravi Patel: the logs we saw show a memory pressure event coincident with a fallback to q3b variant, that created more GC and delayed response. can you share pod logs?
[03:37] Avery Singh: yes that's one of the action items.
[03:40] Marta Ruiz: one more question on cost - how does committed slot pricing break out vs pay-as-you-go?
[03:46] Emma Castillo: we'll send a committed slot estimate; high level: committed reduces per-token price by ~30% for the slot baseline, burst is billed at on-demand rates. i'll include a simple example sheet.
[03:57] Jon Park: curious about the evening variance - can you run specifically a latency-only run with pinned model and full trace (95th p95 with sampling) so we can see exact tail behavior?
[04:06] Ravi Patel: yes, that's our recommendation as well — separate latency test without aggressive batching, and we capture full traces, we can run that overnight and post results.
[04:13] Marta Ruiz: timeline? we need results before next week steering committee on 1/6.
[04:18] Emma Castillo: we'll aim to have the tuned config and the latency-only results by 2027-01-04, that gives you time to review.
[04:25] Lena Cho: great, and can you put the config in a runbook so our SRE can test it locally?
[04:29] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll provide a runbook with exact flags: batch_window_ms, target_batch_count, kv_cache_prefix_keep, quant_profile, and fallback thresholds.
[04:37] Noah Kim: also pro-tip: enabling continuous prefix prewarm during your controlled ramp reduced p95 by ~18% in our internal tests.
[04:45] Jon Park: small nit — the transcription in the shared notes spelled KV as K-V cash, just throwing it out, lol.
[04:51] (laughter)
[04:54] Emma Castillo: any blockers on the legal/security side that would prevent us from starting a short dedicated pilot?
[05:01] Marta Ruiz: legal flagged data residency but we can sign a DPA if keys remain in our KMS. need security brief though.
[05:08] Emma Castillo: we'll send the security brief and DPA template.
[05:11] Ravi Patel: final technical note — for the throughput profile we disabled strict prefix caching which allowed higher tokens/sec but worsened p95 on cold misses; the balanced profile kept a 4ms batching window and modest prewarm, that tends to be best for mixed workload.
[05:27] Avery Singh: can we also see the flamegraphs / kernel utilization? might explain the evening latency spikes.
[05:33] Ravi Patel: yes we'll add kernel ugraphs and nvlink stats to the upload.
[05:37] Emma Castillo: ok let's recap next steps and owners — ravi will upload configs and traces, emma to send pricing estimate and DPA, marta/avery to share logs and prompt set.
[05:49] Marta Ruiz: thanks everyone.
[05:51] Jon Park: thanks.
[05:52] Lena Cho: i'll hop off but thanks, good session.
[05:55] Noah Kim: we'll schedule the security deep dive for next week, i'll propose two slots after the call.
[05:59] Emma Castillo: great, meeting adjourned.
